newsitem.title: UK: Price reversal may fuel Latam oil sector downturn.
newsitem.headline: Price reversal may fuel Latam oil sector downturn.

text.p: Latin America's oil sector, powering ahead on the back of higher oil prices, may consolidate its gains in the short term but is vulnerable to the chance of a price correction next year, Kleinwort Benson analysts said.

In a note to investors outlining its expectations for third quarter results across Latam's energy sector, Kleinwort Benson analysts said on Tuesday the sector was likely to face a quieter period of consolidation.

"The Latin American oil sector has rebounded 11 percent since July driven by current high oil prices," oil and gas analyst Kerry Bernal said. "In the short term we expect the sector to consolidate gains."
But longer term the picture was likely to change.
"Looking further ahead, the oil producers appear vulnerable to our expectation of an oil price correction in 1997."

The bank said it had altered its ratings for a number of Latin American oil companies, upgrading Argentina's Astra Capsa to "Buy", and downgrading its Transportadora de Gas del Sur and Metrogas to "Hold".
An aggressive expansion plan by Astra, in which Spain's Repsol SA has a controlling stake, involving a $1.0 billion capital expenditure programme, aims to triple Astra's profits by 2000, it said.
In contrast, it estimated that TGS was the most sensitive to higher corporate tax charges introduced retrospectively on September 30.
"The charge...eats into Q3 earnings causing a nine percent fall year on year," Bernal said.
Metrogas' downgrade was due to a 1996 year-on-year earnings estimate 15 percent below last year's, following a warm August and the reversal of a 5.0 million peso tax credit.

In Brazil, congress continues to scrutinise deregulation law. Kleinwort Benson expects a series of write-downs on Petrobras's debt to negatively affect earnings; however it saw important long term benefits from deregulation.
"Upstream should see a spree of joint ventures with international oil companies while downstream price regulation should eliminate the cash flow leak into alcohol subsidies," it said.
In Argentina, Bernal forecast production doubling to 10 percent for 1996, despite an expected decline in production in the fourth quarter.

Details of marginal field auctions in Venezuela should be announced this month and she said all Argentine oil companies were expected to participate, although terms may be steeper after a huge response to the last exploration bidding round.
She noted that $16.6 billion is expected to be invested in Colombia's oil and gas sector between 1996 and 2000, out of a total $30 billion budget also earmarked for electricity and infrastructure.
